chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever does an evil deed is given a respite of seven hours of the day. If he says: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, besides Whom there is no god, the Living, the Eternal,' three times, it will not be recorded for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific dhikr and time frame for erasing a sin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the Shia emphasis on the immediacy of repentance, suggesting that a brief, sincere interval of seven hours is sufficient to erase a sin through the recitation of the *Dhikr of Yunus*. The specific formula invokes Allah as 'The Living, The Sustainer,' linking the act of forgiveness to divine vitality and power, a theme central to Shia devotional practices. It underscores the mercy of God in providing a narrow but accessible window for spiritual rectification before the sin is permanently recorded.
